title: Schedule of Financing Classes — Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts
content:
Each account within the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts is held in one of seven financing classes at a time. For each class the schedule fixes how the employer finances benefits, how its contribution rate is set, the industry-code prefix that marks a construction employer, and the consecutive months of liability, ending on the computation date, after which a new employer moves to an experience-rated class.

## Schedule

| Financing class | Financing method | How the contribution rate is set | Construction NAICS prefix | Months of liability before experience rating |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Contributory — New Employer Standard Rate | Contributory | Fixed new employer rate | 23 | 24 |
| Contributory — New Employer Construction Rate | Contributory | Fixed new employer rate | 23 | 24 |
| Contributory — Experience-Rated Positive Reserve | Contributory | Reserve-ratio schedule | 23 | 0 |
| Contributory — Experience-Rated Deficit Reserve | Contributory | Reserve-ratio schedule | 23 | 0 |
| Contributory — Delinquent Reporting Assigned Rate | Contributory | Assigned delinquency rate | 23 | 0 |
| Reimbursing — Nonprofit Organization | Reimbursing | Not applicable — no contribution rate | 23 | 0 |
| Reimbursing — Governmental Entity | Reimbursing | Not applicable — no contribution rate | 23 | 0 |

A figure of 0 in the last column means the class is not a new-employer class.

## Who each class holds

- **Contributory — New Employer Standard Rate** — a contributory employer with fewer months of liability than 24 whose NAICS code does not begin with 23.
- **Contributory — New Employer Construction Rate** — a contributory employer with fewer months of liability than 24 whose NAICS code begins with 23.
- **Contributory — Experience-Rated Positive Reserve** — a contributory, experience-rated employer whose reserve ratio at the computation date is zero or more.
- **Contributory — Experience-Rated Deficit Reserve** — a contributory, experience-rated employer whose reserve ratio at the computation date is below zero.
- **Contributory — Delinquent Reporting Assigned Rate** — a contributory, experience-rated employer with quarterly reports missing at the computation date.
- **Reimbursing — Nonprofit Organization** — a 501(c)(3) nonprofit with a reimbursing election on file, keeping the security set for the class.
- **Reimbursing — Governmental Entity** — a governmental entity with a reimbursing election on file.

## Reading the schedule

- *Contributory* employers pay contributions on taxable wages at a rate; *reimbursing* employers pay back the benefits charged to them instead and have no contribution rate.
- The construction prefix, 23, is compared with the beginning of the employer's NAICS code; it is what separates the two new-employer classes.

**Hypothetical illustration.** Two contributory employers each have 10 months of liability. One carries NAICS code 238220, which begins with 23, and sits in Contributory — New Employer Construction Rate; the other carries NAICS code 541211 and sits in Contributory — New Employer Standard Rate. Both have fewer months of liability than 24, so neither has yet reached experience rating.
